user_questions.question: Two intent questions. (1) The org already has Contact.Loyalty_Tier__c (restricted picklist) with values Explorer, Insider, Pronto Plus, Pronto One, Pronto Elite; your requirement says Plus, One, Elite. Options: (a) keep the existing values as-is, zero change [recommended; AgentGetLoyaltyTierActions, Data Cloud and Slack read them]; (b) change only the labels to Plus/One/Elite, keeping API values; (c) rename the API values too, with a data update. (2) All 198 Contacts have a blank tier. Options: (a) leave blank until real tiers are known [recommended]; (b) backfill Explorer as a data step; (c) you supply tier data to load.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Just the tier value on the customer. (Q1 mapped to option a as an assumption; Q2 not covered: No preference; use your recommended default.)

skill_friction: Step 4 says always send I, but when discovery already shows the requirement is met (zero-change), the I call adds latency (132 s here) and only returns 'No metadata changes are required.' plus irrelevant alternatives; the skill could allow skipping I for a verified already-met case, as it does for R and T.

Step 5 'Before asking, predict the answer' vs 'a change that alters behavior for other callers of a shared component': the Pronto-prefix label mismatch sits on both sides (a safe zero-change default exists, yet the requirement wording differs from org values). Unclear whether a naming mismatch between requirement and existing values is a question or a decide-yourself case.

No guidance on what an answer like 'Just the tier value on the customer' that confirms scope but ignores the options should be tagged as: user decision for scope vs assumption for the option mapping; I split it, but the rule only covers mapping to one option.
AskCoworker labelled facts it got from my message as '[Verified: ... prior session]'; the memory rule handles this, but echoed facts carry misleading provenance labels.
FieldPermissions returned no profile rows (not even System Administrator) for the field; org-verification.md does not say how to interpret or report profile-level access when no rows appear.
